#2502. Feyenoord stretch lead ahead of Eredivisie top clash against PSV

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Feyenoord have opened up a three-point lead at the top of the Eredivisie ahead of next weekend’s clash with PSV, following the defending champions’ shock defeat at ADO Den Haag.

The Rotterdammers were made to work for their points in a seven-goal thriller at Telstar.

They took the lead after just 25 seconds when Gaoussou Diarra finished off a sweeping move and were 3-1 up after 32 minutes when Sem Steijn profited from good combination work by Gjivai Zechiël and Givairo Read.

Patrick Brouwer reduced the deficit five minutes later, but a second-half penalty by Steijn proved to be enough despite Noach Shenkman scoring a third for Telstar on 69 minutes.

Peter Bosz refused to blame the last-minute defeat at ADO on his injury crisis as he looks ahead to a testing week, with a trip to Porto in the Champions League on Tuesday followed by the visit of Feyenoord on Sunday.

PSV looked to be on course for a routine win when Sven Mijnans put them ahead in the 21st minute. But the midfielder’s dismissal just before half-time triggered a second-half collapse that culminated in Matej Sin’s headed winner for ADO in the 93rd minute.

Mijnans, who played as a makeshift striker, will be suspended for the game against Feyenoord, while Guus Til also went off after complaining of blurred vision after landing hard on his neck in the first half and is doubtful for the next week.

But Bosz said he did not fear his team was sliding into a “tricky situation” in the absence of other senior players such as Jerdy Schouten, Ricardo Pepi and new signing Sami Ouaissa.

“This is another chance to win a game,” he said. “Stick our chests out and not think in fear.”

AZ Alkmaar also dropped points against a newly promoted club as they could only draw 2-2 with Cambuur Leeuwarden even after the Friesland club lost Devid Bouah to a second yellow card early in the second half.

Twente Enschede missed the chance to leap into second place as Spanish striker Ángel Alarcón scored two superb goals for Utrecht to lift Anthony Correia’s team to 11th place.

Julian Brandt and Jorthy Mokio both scored twice as Ajax won 5-2 in Groningen in a match that saw both goalkeepers save penalties.

A double by Anthony Descotte looked to have earned Fortuna Sittard the points at NEC until Willum Thór Willumsson popped up with an injury-time header to snatch a draw for the struggling Nijmegen club.

#2499. INTERVIEW: Makaay not concerned with Bayern's striker depth, holds squad among Champions League favourites

MÜNCHEN (Bulinews) Roy Makaay is not concerned about the lack of depth at striker in Vincent Kompany's squad. The former FC Bayern marksman believes several players can cover for Harry Kane in the event of an emergency.

“I haven’t spoken with Harry [Kane] about it, but I don’t think he likes to be on the bench that often. Kompany has given him some rest [here and there] which is perfect," Makaay told Bulinews.com and other media at a round table event.

“If the game [result] is clear, you can almost give him the day off. I think [the lack of depth at striker] is why they signed [Ismael] Saibari as well. I know Saibari from the Dutch league, he was really amazing last season.

“He can play several positions. Of course, he prefers to play the number 10 role, but for the Moroccan national team he is the striker. I think [Serge] Gnabry has played as a striker for the [German] national team as well.

“Last year, they had solutions like [Nicolas] Jackson, this year that’s why they bought Saibari because he can cover a lot [of positions]. Luis Diaz was maybe the only one on the left wing, even if Phonzie Davies can play there.

“Last year, he [Davies] was injured as well, so with the signings of [Nathaniel] Brown and Saibari there are more possibilities to replace Harry Kane if he needs a rest,” the 51-year-old double Bundesliga winner explained.

Delving into the UEFA Champions League and Bayern's chances of picking up the title for the first time since 2020, Makaay believes the German record champions are right in the mix but may need some good fortune in the knockout draw.

“They are one of the top teams like Paris [Saint-Germain]. Like last season, it’s the most difficult [competition] to win because you have 5 or 6 teams who could win it,” said Makaay, who was unlucky not to lift the trophy in his playing career.

“It depends a little bit on the draw because all the big teams were on one side like Man City, Real Madrid, Liverpool, Bayern and PSG. Of course, the first goal for Bayern is making the top 8 to avoid the extra [qualifying] game.

“Sure, you need a little bit of luck in the draw [for the knockouts] as well, but I can see them winning it. Of course, PSG, Real Madrid, Barcelona are playing really well, but [Bayern] have the team to win it,” he concluded.

#2498. England’s Dutch coach Sarina Wiegman extends contract until 2029

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Dutch football coach Sarina Wiegman has extended her contract with the England women’s team by two years, taking her up to the 2029 European Championships.

Wiegman, 56, led the team to two European titles in 2022 and 2025, as well as their first World Cup final in 2023, when they lost to Spain.

Prior to that she won the European Championships with the Dutch national team in 2017 and reached the World Cup final two years later, losing 2-0 to the United States.

“I am so happy to be able to carry on with this squad and cannot think of a better job in football,” she said in a statement released by the English Football Association (FA).

“Working for a world-class organisation like the FA, and alongside so many people dedicated to winning England teams and the growth of our game, excites me every day.”

FA chief executive Mark Bullingham described Wiegman as “an incredible coach with an unparalleled record in major tournaments”. He added: “There is no one better to lead the Lionesses into the next two tournaments.”

Commentators had widely expected the Dutchwoman to leave her post after next year’s World Cup, after England failed to qualify automatically for the tournament.

A 4-0 loss to Spain in June, the team’s heaviest defeat since Wiegman took charge, means they will have to come through a play-off tournament with Greece, Ukraine and Slovakia to reach the finals in Brazil.

Wiegman said: “Anyone who knows me will understand that my main concern right now is absolutely the World Cup, and helping this squad realise their potential in the years to come.

“We have an important job to do to confirm our place in Brazil, and hopefully we can do that and give the country another special summer to remember next year.”

#2497. Paolo Zanetti è il nuovo allenatore dell'Udinese

Dopo l'esonero di Kosta Runjaic, l'Udinese ha ufficializzato l'arrivo del nuovo allenatore

Dopo l'esonero di Kosta Runjaic, l'Udinese ha ufficializzato l'arrivo del nuovo allenatore, Paolo Zanetti.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Udinese Calcio è lieta di annunciare di aver affidato a Paolo Zanetti la guida tecnica della prima squadra. Ha firmato un contratto fino al 30 giugno 2027.Nato a Valdagno, in provincia di Vicenza, il 16 dicembre 1982, Zanetti vanta una carriera da calciatore, durante la quale ha vestito, tra le altre, le maglie di Torino e Atalanta, collezionando anche cinque presenze con la Nazionale Under 21. Appesi gli scarpini al chiodo, ha intrapreso immediatamente la carriera da allenatore, guidando la formazione Berretti della Reggiana a soli 33 anni. Il suo percorso nel calcio professionistico inizia nella stagione 2017/2018 alla guida del Südtirol, con cui ottiene risultati importanti che, dopo due stagioni a Bolzano, gli valgono la chiamata dell’Ascoli in Serie B. La stagione della consacrazione è la 2020/2021, quando conduce il Venezia alla promozione in Serie A, riportando i lagunari nella massima serie dopo 19 anni di assenza. Zanetti resta sulla panchina del Venezia anche nella stagione successiva, prima di trasferirsi all’Empoli, con cui conquista una tranquilla salvezza nell’annata 2022/2023. La sua ultima esperienza in Serie A è quella sulla panchina del Verona, squadra che conduce al quattordicesimo posto nella stagione 2024/2025 e con cui rimane fino al febbraio 2026.Ora per Paolo Zanetti si apre una nuova sfida: guidare l’Udinese e iniziare un nuovo capitolo della sua carriera in bianconero.Il nuovo allenatore dirigerà domani pomeriggio la prima seduta di allenamento. La conferenza stampa di presentazione si terrà mercoledì alle ore 15.00.A mister Zanetti e a tutto il suo gruppo di lavoro va il caloroso benvenuto da parte dell’intero club.Benvenuto a Udine, mister!

#2495. PSV hold on to book narrow Champions League win in Porto

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

PSV survived a second-half onslaught in Porto to secure their first win of the Champions League group stages.

Guus Til scored the only goal when he tapped in from close range after Esmir Bajraktarevic’s shot had come back off the post and was steered across goal by Sven Mijnans.

The Eindhoven club were worth their narrow lead against Francesco Farioli’s side after dominating possession in the first half, but rarely troubled Diogo Costa in the Porto goal.

Til went close with a header early in the second half before putting PSV ahead in the 57th minute.

But the visitors had to defend heroically as Porto poured forward in search of an equaliser, aided by an increasingly fragile Matej Kovar.

The goalkeeper put his defenders in jeopardy with a weak clearance in the 72nd minute, but redeemed himself by saving Victor Froholdt’s shot with his chest before Lutsarel Geertruida blocked the follow-up from Pepê.

A minute later Kovar was left stranded after he rushed out of his penalty area, but Sergiño Dest managed to hack the ball away before Alberto Costa could poke it into the open goal.

At the other end, substitute Denis Man came close to scoring a second for PSV with his first touch when his curling shot beat Costa but failed to sneak inside the post.

The 1-0 win lifts PSV to a provisional 16th place in the Champions League table at the halfway stage of round three, while Porto are still looking for their first point.

Their next match is at home to Belgian side Club Brugge, who will make the short trip to Eindhoven on November 4.

#2494. Klopp settles Germany's goalkeeping debate ahead of November fixtures

Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp named three goalkeepers in his squad for the upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures against Serbia and the Netherlands, which was announced on Thursday: Marc-André ter Stegen (Ajax), Jonas Urbig (Bayern Munich) and Alexander Nübel (Besiktas).

After rotating between the three in his first four matches in charge last month, Klopp has now confirmed that ter Stegen remains Germany's clear first-choice goalkeeper.

“Marc is having a fantastic season in Amsterdam, and fortunately, the other two [Urbig and Nübel] are also having really good seasons. We're going into these matches with Marc as our number one,” Klopp said in an interview with DFB.tv (via iMiaSanMia).

"And this isn't about who happens to be making the better saves at any given moment, because goalkeepers need to provide a lot of stability and confidence. The number one requirement for a goalkeeper is to make sure the ball doesn't end up in the net. That's the most important thing. But beyond that, there are several other aspects that matter: How can he dictate our game, including when we're in possession? How does he handle these situations? And when we're defending with a high line, how early can he recognise those situations so that he can defend further up the pitch as a goalkeeper?

"It's a strange way of putting it, but essentially, it's about knowing when to come out and deal with the danger – not trying to dribble, but simply clearing the ball. All of these things are part of the job. Marc has the most experience in this area, and, yes, we're going into these matches with him as our number one."

Germany face Serbia away from home on November 13 before hosting the Netherlands three days later.

#2492. Cragnotti critica la protesta dei tifosi Lazio all’Olimpico

L’ex presidente, tornato allo stadio per la vittoria sul Cagliari, distingue la contestazione a Lotito dal sostegno alla squadra.

Sergio Cragnotti non condivide la protesta dei tifosi Lazio che lascia vuoti gli spalti dell’Olimpico. L’ex presidente biancoceleste è tornato allo stadio per assistere alla vittoria contro il Cagliari e ha preso posizione sulla contestazione a Claudio Lotito. Sulla scelta di non sostenere la squadra in casa il suo giudizio è netto: «Sono in totale disaccordo».

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Cragnotti, intervistato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, non mette in discussione il diritto dei sostenitori di manifestare il proprio dissenso. «Le contestazioni ci possono stare, io ne ho subite anche di dure», ha spiegato. A non convincerlo è la decisione di lasciare vuoti gli spalti mentre la Lazio continua a vincere.

Per l’ex presidente, la contrarietà alla società dovrebbe trovare spazio in altre sedi, senza togliere ai calciatori l’appoggio del pubblico all’Olimpico. A suo giudizio, l’assenza dei tifosi rischia di penalizzare proprio i giocatori protagonisti di un avvio che considera straordinario.

Nel motivare la propria posizione, Cragnotti è tornato alle proteste vissute durante la sua presidenza. Tra gli episodi ricordati c’è la contestazione legata alla possibile cessione di Giuseppe Signori al Parma.

Furono momenti di forte tensione, ma, secondo il ricordo dell’ex presidente, i sostenitori non abbandonarono mai l’Olimpico. È questa la differenza che Cragnotti individua rispetto all’attuale forma di protesta: contestare la società senza far mancare la presenza allo stadio.

Feyenoord endured a frustrating evening in Spain as a penalty by Real Betis’s outstanding player, Isco, secured a 1-0 win for the La Liga side.

#2490. Pinamonti segna e pesa: il 52% dei suoi gol è stato decisivo

Il gol al Cagliari aggiorna il bilancio: dal 2021/22, 26 delle sue 50 reti in Serie A hanno inciso sul risultato.

Non conta soltanto quanto segna un attaccante, ma anche quanto incidono le sue reti. Andrea Pinamonti offre una fotografia significativa sotto questo aspetto: dalla stagione 2021/22, il 52% dei suoi gol in Serie A è risultato decisivo.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Il centravanti ha realizzato 26 reti decisive su 50 complessive, contribuendo a un saldo di 38 punti. Nel conteggio rientra anche il gol del definitivo 2-1 della Lazio contro il Cagliari.

Il periodo analizzato parte dal 2021/22, stagione nella quale l’attaccante classe 1999 ha raggiunto per la prima volta la doppia cifra di reti in Serie A.

Da allora, più della metà dei suoi gol ha avuto un peso sul risultato. Il dato dei 38 punti va letto secondo il criterio indicato nella rilevazione: rappresenta la differenza rispetto ai punti che le sue squadre avrebbero ottenuto sottraendo le reti considerate decisive.

Una statistica che mette in evidenza l’incisività del centravanti e aggiunge una chiave di lettura al suo rendimento realizzativo.

Il contributo più consistente arriva dall’esperienza al Sassuolo: 25 gol complessivi, dei quali 13 decisivi, per un totale di 20 punti attribuiti alle sue marcature.

Con l’Empoli, Pinamonti ha invece firmato 13 reti: 7 decisive, con un’incidenza di 10 punti. Al Genoa, il bilancio riportato è di 10 gol, dei quali 5 decisivi, per 6 punti.

Tre esperienze che, insieme ai primi numeri in biancoceleste, compongono il totale delle 50 reti prese in esame.

Il capitolo Lazio conta finora 2 gol, con una rete decisiva e 2 punti attribuiti alle marcature dell’attaccante.

A incidere è il sigillo del 2-1 contro il Cagliari: sottraendo quella rete, il risultato sarebbe stato un pareggio. Da qui la differenza tra il punto della parità e i tre della vittoria.

Per Pinamonti, dunque, una rete che alimenta il bottino personale e soprattutto sposta il risultato della squadra. È proprio questo il filo conduttore della statistica: 26 volte su 50, i suoi gol hanno fatto la differenza.

#2488. Fantasy Bundesliga tips: 10 players to consider for Matchday 9

In this Fantasy Bundesliga article, we’ll highlight 10 players to consider adding to your team ahead of Matchday 9.

As a rule of thumb, we'll try to steer clear of the most obvious picks, instead focusing mainly on players who could offer great value as differentials.

Koki Machida, Hoffenheim (Defender, 4.1M, 5%)

Coming up against a Schalke side who have managed just four Bundesliga goals this season, Machida offers solid clean-sheet potential at a budget-friendly price.

Miro Muheim, Hamburger SV (Defender, 9.95M, 8%)

Operating out of position in central midfield, Muheim has already shown his explosive potential this season, racking up 315 points against Hoffenheim and 289 against VfB Stuttgart. With HSV hosting bottom-placed Gladbach, the 28-year-old looks like an intriguing differential for Friday night's fixture.

Nathaniel Brown, FC Bayern (Defender, 14.85M, 9%)

After coming off the bench against both Borussia Dortmund and Atletico Madrid, Brown looks set to return to the starting XI against Bayern this weekend, with the German champions expected to rotate their squad amid a packed fixture schedule. The German international could even feature in a more advanced role on the left wing.

Albert Grønbæk, Hamburger SV (Midfielder, 6.99M, 1%)

Although Hamburger SV lost 3-1 to Eintracht Frankfurt last week, Grønbæk still managed to pick up a respectable 122 points. The Danish international operates in a very advanced role – almost as a striker – and with HSV now facing a much more favourable home fixture against a Gladbach side yet to win away from home this season, he's an interesting midfield option at a relatively low price.

Can Uzun, Eintracht Frankfurt (Midfielder, 15.94M, 2%)

Following criticism from head coach Adi Hütter over his mentality and two consecutive starts on the bench, Uzun has worked his way back into the Eintracht line-up and really delivered. He was arguably their standout performer against HSV last weekend and could be influential once more against newly-promoted Paderborn.

Lennart Karl, FC Bayern (Midfielder, 16.34M, 2%)

After coming under criticism for his early-season performances, Karl responded in style with a crucial goal in Bayern's 2-0 win over Atletico Madrid on Tuesday. With Bayern dealing with a lengthy injury list in attack, the 18-year-old looks set to retain his place in the No. 10 role against Mainz, offering an opportunity to build on his impressive mid-week performance.

Konstantinos Karetsas, Borussia Dortmund (Midfielder, 15.18M, 4%)

The Greek youngster gave Dortmund a real boost off the bench in their 2-1 win over Real Betis on Wednesday, scoring the winner. After that performance, you'd expect Karetsas to start this weekend's favourable fixture against Elversberg, but be aware that his minutes could still be managed following his recent injury spell.

Fabio Silva, Borussia Dortmund (Striker, 9.52M, 1%)

Silva built on his goal against Bayern Munich by scoring and providing an assist against Real Betis in the Champions League on Wednesday. Since Serhou Guirassy picked up a knock in that game, the striker even looks likely to play as the front man at home against newly-promoted Elversberg.

Fisnik Asllani, Hoffenheim (Striker, 12.63M, 1%)

Asllani appears to be the most likely starter in Hoffenheim's attack as Christian Ilzer's side look to pick up three much-needed points against struggling Schalke 04 this weekend. The 24-year-old is still working his way back to his best after a spell on the sidelines, but is certainly capable of making a difference, as he showed last season with 11 goals and 10 assists in all competitions.

Igor Matanovic, Freiburg (Striker, 16.59M, 14%)

Union Berlin have conceded heavily in several away fixtures this season, suffering defeats to Leverkusen (4-0), Bayern (7-0) and Köln (5-0). Matanovic will be hoping to exploit the defensive frailties the capital club have shown this season and add to his tally of four Bundesliga goals at the weekend.

Tredici punti in sei giornate: nel periodo considerato dall’arrivo di Raffaele Palladino, il Bologna avrebbe il secondo rendimento del campionato. Secondo quanto riportato da TuttoMercatoWeb, Davanti ai rossoblù ci sarebbe soltanto la Lazio. Il confronto riguarda le ultime sei gare, non la classifica complessiva di Serie A, nella quale il Bologna deve ancora recuperare terreno per avvicinarsi alle posizioni europee.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Subentrato a Domenico Tedesco sulla panchina rossoblù, Palladino ha dato continuità ai risultati di una squadra che nella prima parte della stagione aveva faticato a trovare una propria identità. I 13 punti del periodo preso in esame equivalgono a 2,16 punti a partita, un passo superato soltanto da quello della formazione biancoceleste.

Sei gare restano un intervallo limitato per formulare valutazioni definitive. Il rendimento, però, descrive il cambio di passo del Bologna e la sua maggiore capacità di raccogliere punti. Al dato si accompagnano prestazioni convincenti e successi che hanno segnato le ultime settimane dei rossoblù.

Da Lecce in avanti, secondo la successione riportata, i rossoblù hanno raccolto quattro vittorie e un pareggio nelle cinque gare successive. #2483. Sports club members becoming less tolerant of homosexuality

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Acceptance of homosexuality in Dutch sports clubs has declined significantly in the last generation, according to a survey of attitudes by the Mulier Institute.

The organisation found that 66% of people had no objection to a fellow member of a sports club being gay, while in 2008 the figure was 85%.

Just over half (55%) of respondents said they had no problem sharing a shower with a gay team-mate of the same sex, which also represented a drop from 73% in 2008.

The Mulier Institute said the findings reflected a social trend that has also been seen in schools, where the proportion of boys aged between 12 and 16 with a positive view of homosexuality has dropped from 40% to 22% since 2021.

The Dutch Olympic Committee NOC*NSF said the findings were “highly regrettable” and pledged to step up its efforts to make sport more inclusive.

But the John Blankenstein Foundation, which campaigns for LGBT emancipation in sport, said it had noticed declining enthusiasm for its workshops and growing numbers of parents who voiced objections.

Karin Blankenstein, who set up the organisation in 2008, told NOS: “I get the sensitivity around transgender people in sport at the top level, but this is about amateur sport.”

#2481. Top five football betting tips and tricks

Football is the world’s most famous sport, and it is the sport of choice of a great many sports punters as well. Especially popular in Europe, betting on football can be an incredibly profitable enterprise, so long as you know how to do it.

Getting started on football betting is far from easy, though. This form of gambling requires dedication, investment, and persistence. As you gain experience, your intuition will improve and you will be able to make more correct predictions.

But experience is not the only thing that can help you become a better football punter. In fact, you can substantially improve your betting strategy by simply following some basic football betting tips.

You might find shopping around boring and unhelpful, but you just have to do it when you search sites for football betting. As you know, the higher the odds, the bigger the payout. What you may have missed, however, is that odds are different at each bookmaker. Having said that, shopping around for the best odds is sensible, as it rewards you with bigger payouts.

In this line of thought, sticking to one bookmaker is virtually pointless. Even if the bookie of your choosing offers the best odds for a number of matches, it is highly unlikely that their odds will remain the best for long.

An obvious one, we know. And yet, you will be surprised by the number of football bettors who wager on football, but do not follow the sport. So, why is it important to follow the action closely?

First of all, by watching football matches, you can take part in the most exciting football betting market – the live betting market. What is more important, however, is that following the action provides an invaluable insight into teams and players’ style, condition, and determination – important factors  to consider when placing a bet.

As you watch more and more games, you will improve your analytic abilities. In time, you will be able to make more accurate predictions about the outcome of different matches, which, of course,  will result in placing more winning bets.

As you know, odds are based on the probability of occurrence of a certain outcome; the higher the odds, the more unlikely it is for that outcome to actually occur. But what happens when the odds offered by the bookmaker represent a probability that is lower than the actual probability of an outcome occurring? In such a situation, you can place what is called a value bet.

If you want to become a professional football punter, you should always search for value when betting, as it leads to huge profits

Favoured by beginners in particular, accumulators are a type of football wager which allows you to bet on as many fixtures as you like. Most commonly, you will be asked to choose a match winner, but as the market is diverse, you may be offered a number of other betting options. What makes accumulators an appealing betting market is the huge potential payout – here, you can stake as little as £1 and have the potential to win more than £500,000, depending on the bookmaker and the number of selected fixtures.

If you find accumulators’ payouts too good to be true, you are right. As a matter of fact, there is a reason for the odds to be set so high – actually winning an accumulator bet, especially one which involves a wide selection of matches, is nearly impossible. You see, all you need for your whole wager to lose is one wrong prediction. For example, if you bet on 10 matches and just one of them goes wrong, your entire accumulator is lost.

To make money by betting on football, avoid betting on accumulators – the risk is simply not worth it.

Finally, if you want to be a successful football punter, learn how not to mix emotions with betting. This is easier said than done, though.

Whenever your favourite team plays, you want them to win, regardless of how (im)possible that may be. If you do not learn how to leave emotions out of betting, however, you are highly likely to put money on your favourite team even if they have no chance of winning the match. Conversely, should you base your bets on hard facts and not on emotions, you increase your chances to win.

Our advice – avoid betting on fixtures that involve one of your favourite teams, that is the easiest way to keep emotions at bay.

#2478. Big wins for PSV and Twente close gap on leaders Feyenoord

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

A late equaliser for Fortuna Sittard in De Kuip proved costly for Feyenoord as PSV and Twente racked up huge victories to move within two points of the Eredivisie leaders.

Feyenoord paid the price for failing to finish off the Limburgers, with Luciano Valente’s 59th-minute goal the only reward for their dominance.

Fortuna equalised with four minutes left when Shiloh ’t Zand, on loan from Feyenoord, was allowed to run through to the penalty area and beat Tjark Ernst with a low shot.

Feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst made no effort to hide his disappointment. “We know that Fortuna are the kind of team who can score from the few attacks they have,” he said. “If you don’t score the goals, things like this can happen.”

Second-placed Ajax are a point behind after a narrow win at home against AZ ended an 11-match winless streak against the Alkmaar club, as Tolu Arokodare’s early header proved decisive.

Twente recorded the biggest win of the weekend with a 9-0 demolition of Excelsior in Rotterdam, with Wout Weghorst scoring four times and Sondre Ørjasaeter notching up five assists.

Excelsior collapsed following the fifth-minute dismissal of Nesto Groen for a reckless high challenge. The home side were 5-0 down at half-time, with Weghorst claiming a hat-trick in the opening 33 minutes.

PSV bagged seven goals in a one-sided encounter with bottom club Willem II, with all the goals coming from different scorers including Ricardo Pepi, who came on in the second half after a six-week absence through injury.

ADO went down 1-0 in Zwolle, with PEC’s Dylan Mbayo scoring the only goal with a first-time finish on the stroke of half-time.

The match between Cambuur Leeuwarden and Go Ahead Eagles was suspended in the 82nd minute after visiting fans threw fireworks onto the pitch.

The clubs agreed with the KNVB not to play the final minutes and allow Cambuur’s 4-0 advantage to stand as the final result.

Go Ahead’s director Jan-Willem van Dop said the club would take action against those responsible: “I am ashamed on behalf a small group of supporters who ruined things for the club and a large hare of the fans in the away end,” he said.

Obiettivi? Il percorso però è lungo, le big sono più abituate a fare punti pesanti, impossibile sottovalutarle. E ci saranno tanti scontri diretti da affrontare. Ma se la Lazio sarà così in alto anche alla vigilia degli ultimi due mesi, allora tutto potrà succedere.

Gattuso? Ha rivitalizzato calciatori forti che non avevano reso secondo il loro valore. Ha un sogno, Gattuso? Conoscendolo, vorrebbe rivedere l’Olimpico pieno. Io sono molto legato al popolo biancoceleste, è fantastico: quando firmai per la Lazio ero felice perché da avversario ero incantato dall’atmosfera di quello stadio e finalmente sarebbe stato il mio campo. Quindi capisco il sogno di Rino, spero riesca a realizzarlo.

#2465. Dual passports issue continues to plague Dutch-based footballers

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Dutch-born footballers who were called up to play for former colonies such as Suriname and Indonesia are still in limbo over their national status, six months after the “passportgate” crisis first flared up.

Suriname’s parliament passed a law in September enabling players who are selected for the national team to gain citizenship automatically.

But the Dutch immigration service IND said the law passed in Suriname made no difference to the rules on dual nationality in the Netherlands.

“The fact that Surinamese nationality has been obtained by legal means is not enough on its own to qualify for one of the exceptional categories under our law,” a spokesman for the Dutch justice ministry told broadcaster NOS.

The law was intended to settle the question of dual nationality for footballers, which arose last March when NAC Breda challenged the eligibility of Go Ahead Eagles defender Dean James.

James took Indonesian citizenship last year after accepting an invitation to play for the national team, but under Dutch dual nationality rules he was required to give up his original passport.

The Dutch football association KNVB launched an investigation into the employment status of players who were called up by countries such as Suriname, Cape Verde and Indonesia. In the meantime it arranged for Dutch-based players to be given temporary work permits so they could keep playing for their clubs.

Losing Dutch nationality also stripped them of their EU citizenship, meaning they would need to obtain visas and meet stricter criteria, such as an annual salary threshold of €600,000, to be eligible to play in the Eredivisie.

Several players have passed up invitations to join the Surinamese squad because of the uncertainty, including Danilho Doekhi of Lazio, Milan van Ewijk of Coventry City and Jayden Oosterwolde of Fenerbahçe.

National team manager Henk Fraser said it was “inexplicable” that players’ livelihoods were being damaged by their desire to play international football.

“Both countries have to get together and clarify the situation,” he told NOS. “This is a straightforward case of people following their hearts and wanting to play for Suriname, but not knowing where they stand.”

Some players said they felt misled by the Surinamese football association, which told them they were playing for the national team on “sports passports” that allowed them to remain Dutch citizens.

Former Feyenoord winger Jean-Paul Boëtius said he only discovered after he was first called up for Suriname last year that he had inadvertently renounced his Dutch citizenship as a result.

Shortly afterwards he received a letter from the city council in Rotterdam telling him to hand in his Dutch passport, which he had recently renewed, because it was no longer valid.

“I now have a sticker in my Surinamese passport that says I have a residency permit allowing me to live in the Netherlands,” he told NOS. “But that’s only for a year. It’s a very difficult situation. I want to become Dutch again. I was born and brought up here.”

#2462. Opinion: The morality of football

Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.

Is football a moral force for good? That was the question of the day, and each of the four guests were asked to discuss various aspects of the debate from financial fairplay to club takeovers by foreign entities to racism.

Nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly. Is there a greater significance to the game we are watching, or is it merely 22 humans kicking a leather ball into a net?

Join Nathan as he elaborates on the most significant takeaways of what was a fascinating discussion on the sport and morality in general.

Football, for some, may be the most poignant reminder of the moral universe in which we live. While debate has raged for centuries regarding the precise origin of moral absolutes and how humans ought to live, it is simply unavoidable to say humanity is often troubled by events surrounding the game we all love so dearly.

In not so distant history, every normal act of human life would have been assigned some degree of moral significance. Every action had inherently moral indicators - for good or for evil. Today, postmodern views of morality dominate. These describe morality as an entirely subjective dimension. In other words, it cannot be pinned down exactly whether behaviors are objectively good or bad. We can only find fault with someone else’s interpretation based on their own unique moral code. Morality is relative to the individual or society.

Yet last night’s dialogue concerning football and human behavior was filled with moral accusations and claims which strongly suggested humans are not content with relativist morality. Indeed, we are at times frightened by and disgusted with what we observe in and around football. Our sense of moral justice is deeply disturbed. But with respect to what exactly?

In responding to the panelist’s questions, I observed a familiar paradigm. Each time I have discussed any aspect of moral behavior, the speculation humans are good or at worst morally neutral animals continually reemerges. This widely accepted presupposition is then followed shortly by disgust at some aspect of human behavior. Almost as if to ask “why are all these good humans behaving so badly?” while ignoring the very real implications of this line of inquiry. A question rendered unanswerable by the insistent a priori assumptions from which it was derived.

If humans are intrinsically beneficent, conscientious, fair, humble, and honest then why is football rife with racism, misogyny, greed, disenfranchisement, lies, cheating, violence, and the hypocrisy to deny the occurrence of any such behaviors except when a rival club is the guilty party? Behaviors which are perpetrated by individual supporters, fanatical groups, club administrations, corporate bodies such as FIFA, political entities, nations, and even the players themselves. No one participating faction is guiltless.

To so blithely sidestep more sufficient explanations for the empirical reality of wickedness in football and in human behavior more generally is not just factually incorrect. It undermines real attempts to understand the root of these behaviors where they might be dealt with more effectively.

To listen to The Moral Maze episode entitled “Football: a moral force for good?” produced by BBC radio and featuring PortuGOAL’s Seleção correspondent Nathan Motz click on this link

Furthermore, in good faith, how successful is a response against heinous evil when those perpetrating it are regarded as behaving in accord with their unique moral ambitions? Humans refuse to accept their indisputably objective moral lacking at a fundamental level. This restricts us from ever doing any more than “stamping out” the alleged impropriety of others – while we ourselves may readily engage in these very same behaviors. Moral relativism cannot account for the moral outrage emanating from all corners of the football world. Is Qatar wrong to perpetrate human rights atrocities or is it allowable because their culture is indifferent? Is hooliganism objectively wrong, or only when someone else’s club is responsible?

The overlooking of our own failings while lashing out at others for theirs is quintessential to the morally fallen nature of humanity itself. Football tells all. There are not good people and bad people. There are only people who both willfully and unintentionally transgress the moral code embedded in each of our hearts. A moral law which can only have ever been given by a moral Lawgiver. Otherwise, it is truly your word against mine as it pertains to the moral validity of all behaviors - even those which may deeply violate your conscience.

Football generates an episodic, semantic, and imagistic description of universal archetypes: good and evil, sacrifice and greed, cruelty and mercy, hero and anti-hero. It speaks to every arc of life’s plotline: tragedy, comedy, victory, defeat, the finite nature of our circumstances. It is one of the preeminent existential dialects alongside religion, visual art, written and spoken language, music, and theatre. Football plucks a primal chord.

As metaphysics have been curtailed to just physics in the modern secular West, football has only elevated our awareness of the often dire moral predicaments of our species. Yet it is clear the moral conversation does not originate on a football pitch. The pitch is but a grand stage upon which moral themes may be observed and critiqued, a mirror held in front of our own soul.

The desire for ultimate purpose, for meaning beyond the material realm, never disappeared in modernity. Arguably, it has only become more desperate as the outcry for ultimate significance comes under more scrutiny and criticism by those who constrain ontological explanations to those accounted for by physics. The severity of the mental health crisis in the West is in no small part explained by the terrifying existential awareness we are cut adrift in an abstract sea of meaningless, hopeless wandering between two oblivions - that before mortal life began and that at mortal life’s end. Let football be one voice which reassures you - there is ultimate meaning and good reasons why football so unsettles our craving for justice.

In a palpable, unavoidable way, football and supporter communities across Europe are encountering moral quandaries. In Portugal, age-old debates between FC Porto and Benfica have routinely been haunted by, in many cases, farcical and cynical hypocrisy. Throughout its history, the FPF has been susceptible to showing partiality to a club, player, or style which ultimately degrades the performance of our beloved Seleção. Deny it all we like, and not one aspect of this reality is changed.

In conclusion, whatever your thoughts or beliefs on the subject of moral significance, its origin, the meaning of life, and how football draws that out, I hope it will be beneficial to examine these matters more deeply. In my zeal, I admit I have not always been prudent to initiate these discussions in a way which respects thoughtful disagreement. It is my hope this effort to bring that discussion to Portuguese football will be well-received and carefully pondered. But I will contentedly listen to those followers who may be genuinely unhappy or unsupportive of this or any other idea about which I write.

The readers of this website and the larger Portuguese football loving world are my people. It is a joy and a responsibility I take seriously whenever I have the opportunity to raise important questions about the Selecao, the game, and our lives in general.

#2461. Feyenoord facing fireworks fine after 3-0 loss to Internazionale

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Feyenoord are facing a heavy fine from European football authorities after fireworks were let off during their Champions League defeat by Internazionale.

Referee Glenn Nyberg suspended the match for several minutes after flares were fired onto the roof from outside De Kuip stadium, damaging the structure. Police later made two arrests.

“It’s obviously not right and it’ll be another fine,” coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst said wearily after the game, which ended in a comprehensive 3-0 defeat for his team.

One flare landed on the pitch despite the club taking measures such as hanging nets from the gantries to stop objects being thrown from the stands. “They’re letting off fireworks from outside now,” Van Bronckhorst said. “What do you do about that?”

Uefa are likely to hit Feyenoord with a fine and could order the club to close parts of the stadium for their next home matches in the competition, against Porto on November 24 and RB Leipzig on January 27.

The club also have a suspended penalty hanging over them from last October, when they were fined €60,000 after fans let off fireworks during the match against Greek club Panathinaikos.

On the pitch, Feyenoord were undone by a classic display of Italian defending and counter-attacking, as Internazionale sat back after taking an eighth-minute lead through Yann Bisseck.

Francesco Pio Esposito headed in a second early in the second half, just as Feyenoord were pushing for an equaliser, before Piotr Zielinski made sure of the win with a shot from 20 metres.

Captain Luciano Valente said the result was “more than deserved” and the visitors had shown more “quality”.

“This defeat was harder to take than the one against Barcelona,” he told Ziggo Sport. “Because we thought going in that we could get something, but we just weren’t good enough.”

Van Bronckhorst said he was not surprised by the difference in class between the teams. “They scored the first goal out of nothing,” he said. “And Inter know better what the game needs at every stage.

“Their players have a lot of experience, they’ve been in the final twice in the last four years. So we’re at a disadvantage.”

Xavi Hernandez has his first win as Netherlands head coach as a Mexx Meerdink double led Oranje to a 2-1 win over Serbia in the Nations League.

Xavi made two changes from the side that drew with Germany as Mexx Meerdink replaced the injured Brian Brobbey up front while Joey Veerman came in for Quinten Timber.

Netherlands dominated from the start but they were forced into an early change when Cody Gakpo suffered a knock and Ruben van Bommel came on.

After half an hour, Crysencio Summerville was clipped in the box and Meerdink made it 1-0 from the penalty spot. It was almost 2-0 before the break but Denzel Dumfries could not convert when through on goal.

Serbia made a double change at the break with Luka Jovic and Dusan Tadic coming on. A minute into the second half, the change worked as Jovic was given space in the box to net after Netherlands failed to clear the ball.

Netherlands went in search of the lead again but Tijjani Reijnders blazed a huge chance over while Ruben van Bommel hit the post. Meerdink did eventually make it 2-1 with a lovely finish after a quick 1-2 with substitute Guus Til.

There was to be no hattrick for Meerdink as he was brought off and Netherlands played the final ten minutes with Til through the middle.

Serbia pressed for a late equaliser but the Netherlands had a golden chance to make it 3-1 when Til found himself in on goal. He had Summerville and Van Bommel to his left but overhit the pass and the later’s finish was too weak to find the net.

The Netherlands held on for the victory which takes them to the top of the group with a clash against Greece next on Thursday.

#2457. Why Bayer Leverkusen's Ibrahim Maza has attracted interest from Arsenal, PSG, Man United and other top clubs

The 2026/27 Bundesliga season is only eight matchdays old, yet there are already some clear early winners. One player who has made another significant leap in his development is Bayer 04 Leverkusen's Ibrahim Maza.

Last season, the midfield talent offered flashes of his ability, though he occasionally struggled with fluctuations in form and had to adapt to unfamiliar roles, such as playing in central midfield. This is hardly surprising, given that it was the Berlin native’s first full season in the Bundesliga.

Maza has since established himself as one of the standout performers of the season so far, delivering impressive displays both as an attacking midfielder and out on the wing.

It is therefore not surprising that the 20-year-old was voted into ninth place in the Young Talent Of The Year election and that there have recently been increasing rumors about him. Clubs including Aston Villa, Arsenal, Manchester United, Tottenham Hotspur, and, most notably, Paris Saint-Germain are reportedly keeping a close eye on him. But what exactly does he bring to the table?

Ibrahim Maza is arguably best suited to the central attacking midfield position. In this role, the Algerian international can dictate the attacking play, set up his teammates in promising positions, and, most importantly, navigate out of tight spaces.

In such situations, he benefits from his significantly improved physical robustness, combined with quick feet and great agility. Paired with his excellent ball control and tricky dribbling, Maza is extremely difficult to dispossess, a fact he has demonstrated impressively on numerous occasions of late.

While Maza can certainly fill in as a wide player or in a deeper central midfield role, his most effective position is as a "number ten," playing just behind Patrik Schick. This is where Maza feels most at home, and he has shown impressive chemistry with the Czech forward this season.

This position also allows him to make the most of his other strengths. Although Maza is quick on his feet and capable of winning duels on the flank thanks to his dribbling ability, he is not the type of "speed-dribbler" seen in players like Lamine Yamal or Yan Diomande. Conversely, a deeper central midfield role doesn't fully play to his strengths, as his focus is primarily on the attacking phase.

In the attacking phase this season, Maza has established himself as both an effective ball-carrier and the creative hub of Leverkusen's attack. Averaging more than three carries per match, he ranks among the best players in his position in the Bundesliga, consistently driving the play forward.

Once in the final third, his remarkable technical ability and high footballing intelligence come to the fore. Maza possesses an intuitive sense for positioning, frequently finding himself in promising scoring positions. It is no coincidence that, among all attacking midfielders, he ranks highly for both shots taken and touches inside the opposition penalty area per game.

Furthermore, from these positions, the German-Algerian is also adept at creating chances for his teammates. More than 1.4 shot assists per game and more than 0.5 smart passes per game are impressive. In addition to his two assists, he also has two pre-assists, which represents an improvement in his goal-scoring threat compared to last season.

Maza is not merely a constant nuisance who poses a direct goal threat; he also consistently demonstrates an eye for his teammates, initiating scoring opportunities and delivering decisive passes. Despite his youth, he has already become a focal point of the Leverkusen attack, regularly driving opposing defenders to distraction with his clever, inventive style of play.

Naturally, there is still room for improvement when it comes to Ibrahim Maza. Aside from his goalscoring output and finishing efficiency, there is little to criticise about his attacking game. He is, after all, a player who can truly make the difference. The situation is different, however, when it comes to his defensive work. Maza could certainly be more tenacious, engage in more duels, and – most importantly – win them with the right level of intensity. Currently, his success rate in ground duels sits at only around 40 percent.

Furthermore, while his creativity and willingness to take risks are assets, he also needs to learn to choose the right moments for such actions. Consequently, there is room for development regarding his decision-making and the number of times he loses possession. At the same time, it is crucial not to stifle his natural joy for the game; the key lies in finding the right balance.

Given his outstanding start to the season, the rumors surrounding this 20-year-old attacking gem come as no surprise. Even during his time at Hertha BSC, Maza was hailed as an exceptional talent; he is simply beginning to realize his full potential more effectively.

Fundamentally, there are several factors Maza should consider when deciding on the next step in his career. To showcase his abilities, he is best suited to a team that prioritizes possession-based football. Furthermore, the club must have a clear role for him, and he needs a realistic prospect of regular playing time. A job-sharing arrangement or a role as a backup is, in all likelihood, not a viable option for him.

Manchester United, meanwhile, may not be the ideal destination for Maza; The Reds are currently grappling with significant issues, and their style of play raises further questions. While Paris Saint-Germain’s footballing philosophy might be a good fit, it is difficult to identify a clear role for him in Luis Enrique's side. There is also speculation that PSG might be looking at Maza as a replacement for Khvicha Kvaratskhelia – who is currently sidelined with a cruciate ligament injury – to play on the wing. Even though a move to PSG might sound enticing, this setup would not be ideal for Maza.

This leaves Arsenal, Aston Villa, and Tottenham Hotspur. However, things are not running entirely smoothly for the team under Roberto De Zerbi (Tottenham), and with the return of Dejan Kulusevski, the presence of James Maddison, and the eventual return of Xavi Simons, there is stiff competition for his position at the club.

The competition is no less intense at Arsenal or Aston Villa. Both clubs possess a wealth of quality in the position Maza plays, meaning the 20-year-old would likely find himself having to wait for his opportunity behind other established players.

Ibrahim Maza undoubtedly has the potential to become a world-class player. If he makes the right decisions about the next steps in his career, he has every chance of reaching that level. In my view, however, none of the clubs currently linked with him offer the right environment; for this reason, I would personally advise against leaving Leverkusen too soon.

At Bayer 04, Maza receives the playing time in his preferred position that he needs for his development. It would therefore be wise for him to remain in Leverkusen at least until next summer before exploring the market for suitable options. A premature departure, by contrast, could, in the worst-case scenario, hinder his development and lead to stagnation.

That said, I believe Maza is capable of holding his own in almost any league. He possesses the necessary technical skills as well as the physical attributes that are particularly in demand in the Premier League. If he fulfils his potential, he could even realise his dream of one day being named on the Ballon d'Or shortlist.

Florian Först is a German scouting expert and the editor-in-chief of Kickfieber.de. He specialises in player analysis and talent scouting, offering insights into the strengths, weaknesses and potential of emerging football talents.

#2455. PSV edged out by sharper Club Brugge in Champions League defeat

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

PSV Eindhoven endured a frustrating night in the Champions League as their defensive frailties were exposed in a 2-1 defeat by Club Brugge.

PSV started full of attacking intent and should have taken an early lead when Ivan Perisic put Sergiño Dest clean through on goal, but the defender’s shot was too close to goalkeeper Yann Sommer.

Instead it was the visitors who took the lead with their first real attack when Nicolo Tresoldi headed in a teasing cross from Joaquin Seys.

PSV equalised early in the second half as an outstanding pass by Sven Mijnans into the path Lutsharel Geertruida allowed the defender to charge to the byline. His pullback found its way to Kodai Sano, whose shot took a deflection off Seys into the net.

But five minutes later PSV were caught out as another razor-sharp pass by Seys released Carlos Forbs in space to net the winner.

The home side refused to give up, but were unable to find a way past Sommer in the closing stages as the Belgian side closed out the win.

Team captain Mauro Junior admitted that PSV had been undone by shortcomings at the back. “We had a lot of opportunities in the first half but we didn’t score,” he told Ziggo Sport.

“We want to attack and score goals, but we weren’ well organised today in defence. We need to keep our heads up and look forward to the next game.”

The result leaves PSV in 24th place, just above the elimination line, ahead of their next match away to Real Madrid on November 24, with four points from their opening four matches.

An injury-hit Netherlands side battled back to draw 2-2 against Greece in the Nations League.

Xavi was forced into changes with Cody Gakpo and Jan Paul van Hecke dropping out of the squad. Tijjani Reijnders and Ryan Gravenberch also dropped to the bench with Quinten Timber, Guus Til, Jurrien Timber and Ruben van Bommel starting.

Greece have been in good form recently and their confidence was clear from the start. They had a goal disallowed for offside before Fotis Ioannidis made it 1-0 after 23 minutes.

The Netherlands offered little going forward and in stoppage time, a bad back pass from Van Bommel led to Giorgos Masouras sliding in a second.

Xavi made a triple change as Gravenberch, Noa Lang and Reijnders came on and they all made a big difference as the Netherlands dominated the second half.

Virgil van Dijk headed one back before Denzel Dumfries had two goals disallowed for offside. Xavi turned to Joshua Zirkzee and debutante Gjivai Zechiel in hope of an equaliser.

The equaliser came in the last minute as Zechiel’s overhead kick dropped into the path of Reijnders who blasted the ball in. Zechiel then came close to a winner but his header was straight at the goalkeeper.

A battling point for the Netherlands, who stay unbeaten under Xavi with a game at home to Serbia to come on Sunday.

The Netherlands came back from 2-0 down to earn a 2-2 draw against Greece in the Nations League. Here is our player ratings for the Netherlands players.

Bart Verbruggen 5.5/10: Wasn’t happy with his defence in the first half. Could have done more for the first goal but did make a good save. Had nothing to do after the break.

Denzel Dumfries 5/10: Struggled in the first half before improving in the second. Had two goals disallowed for offside.

Micky van de Ven 5/10: His pace makes up for the gaps he leaves at times and in the firs half he struggled. Like others he got better in the second but had less to do.

Jurrien Timber 4/10: Looked very much like a player who is not fully fit. Second to everything and gave away fouls in the first half. Was too slow too react for the second goal.

Virgil van Dijk 6/10: Defensively he struggled in the first but his goal got his side back into the game after the break.

Joey Veerman 6.5/10: Always looking to make something happen going forward. Not everything worked but was always available. His corner led to a goal an he almost scored a free kick.

Quinten Timber 4/10: Disastrous display as he gave away foul after foul in the first half. Was rightly hooked at half time.

Guus Til 4/10: Like Timber, he offered nothing in the first half and was rightly taken off. Xavi wanted to give him a chance but he didn’t take it.

Crysencio Summerville 6/10: Was Netherlands only outlet going forward in the first half and is a constant threat on the right hand side.

Ruben van Bommel 4.5/10: Was too static at times and his error led to the second goal. Taken off at the break.

Mexx Meerdink 5/10: Tried but was isolated at times. Had no service in the first half and barely touched the ball in the second.

Noa Lang 7/10: Offered more on the left than Van Bommel as he took the game to the Greek defence. His cross led to the equaliser. Likely to start against Serbia after this display.

Tijjani Reijnders 6.5/10: Came on and scored the equaliser with a good finish. Did a lot more running than Til did and it was much needed energy.

Ryan Gravenberch 6.5/10: Immediately helped the Netherlands midfield gain control back in the second half.

Joshua Zirkzee N/A: Not on the pitch long enough for a review

Netherlands edged out Serbia 2-1 in Eindhoven to move top of their Nations League group.

Xavi decided to name Teun Koopmeiners in the starting eleven but at centre-back alongside Virgil van Dijk, who was earning his 100th cap. Ryan Gravenberch, Tijjani Reijnders and Noa Lang all came into the eleven.

Netherlands made a strong start and missed two good chances to take the lead within the first two minutes. They then dominated possession but it took until the 31st minute for Oranje to take the lead. Koopmeiners free kick evaded everyone and nestled in the corner.

Oranje were only ahead for four minutes as Mihaijo Cvetkovic was allowed far too much space in the Netherlands box to loop in a header. It could have been worse for the Netherlands before the break but Pavlovic squandered a chance when in on goal.

Xavi brought on Joshua Zirkzee for Mexx Meerdink at the break but the best chances early in the second half were for Serbia. Cvetkovic should have put the visitors ahead.

Xavi turned to the bench again with Gjivai Zechiel, Ruben van Bommel and Jorrel Hato all appearing. Reijnders should have made it 2-1 but when through on goal he scooped the ball over the bar.

Netherlands retook the lead after 72 minutes with Denzel Dumfries crossing for Reijnders to square it to an unmarked Zirkzee, who tapped in. It should have been 3-1 straight away but Reijnders was denied through on goal.

The Netherlands sat back and that allowed Serbia to put on pressure. That pressure increased when Micky van de Ven was forced off and Oranje played the last five minutes with only ten men.

Bart Verbruggen made a big save to deny Nemanja Gudelj and Netherlands managed to hold on for the three points.

Netherlands first four games under Xavi see them win two and draw two. They will finish the Nations League at home to Germany and then away to Greece.

FT Netherlands 2-1 SerbiaIt’s three points but far from convincing in the end. Xavi remains unbeaten in his first four games in charge

#2444. Pancaro: “L'unica cosa che non deve fare la Lazio è quella di mettersi pressione”

Dall'avvio da record alla gestione della pressione: l'analisi di Giuseppe Pancaro sulla straordinaria partenza biancoceleste.

Giuseppe Pancaro, intervenuto ai microfoni di Radiosei, ha analizzato il super momento della Lazio: la forza del gruppo, i successi senza pubblico e la gestione saggia degli obiettivi futuri.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Come sto vivendo questo momento Lazio? E' una Lazio bellissima, non è un momento. Ventotto punti in 10 gare non è un caso. C'è del valore, grande merito da parte di Gattuso. Finalmente anche la soddisfazione per i tifosi che da anni non sognavano più e adesso stanno gioendo.

Ancora più sorprendente fare questi risultati senza tifosi all'Olimpico? Questo è un ulteriore merito di questo gruppo perché la difficoltà ambientale è oggettiva da anni. La sensazione è che loro ora non avvertano questo problema. Sicuramente giocare una gara come quella col Cagliari davanti a 13000 spettatori rispetto ad uno stadio pieno qualcosa toglie sempre. Questa squadra è talmente forte, concentrata, unita e compatta che riesce ad andare oltre.

C'è un momento in ogni stagione in cui ci si accorge che l'obiettivo postosi è cambiato. Quale sarà questo momento in cui magari dai 40 punti si passa a pensare ad una coppa europea? Gattuso in tal senso è bravissimo. L'unica cosa che non deve fare la Lazio è quella di mettersi pressione. Eventualmente penso se ne possa parlare in primavera, al momento fanno benissimo a giocare pensando ad una gara alla volta senza mettersi addosso pressione.

#2443. « Il est en pleine confiance, comme moi » : Moïse Kouamé prêt à défier un cador au Rolex Paris Masters !

À peine auréolé de son tout premier titre sur le circuit Challenger en Bretagne, Moïse Kouamé s'apprête à disputer un premier tour de gala ce mardi 3 novembre 2026. Le joueur tricolore affronte en effet l'Espagnol Alejandro Davidovich Fokina au premier tour du Rolex Paris Masters, à la Plenitude Arena.

Dimanche 1er novembre 2026, Moïse Kouamé a frappé un grand coup en remportant la finale du tournoi Challenger de Brest contre Martin Damm (6-4, 6-7 [5], 7-6 [4]) au terme d'un âpre combat de 2h18 de jeu. Une performance retentissante. À seulement 17 ans et 7 mois, le joueur originaire de Sarcelles est ainsi devenu le troisième plus jeune Français titré à ce niveau derrière Richard Gasquet et Fabrice Santoro, ainsi que le plus précoce depuis 2003.

D'ailleurs, cette ascension fulgurante porte la marque de son mentor. Entraîné par Richard Gasquet en personne, l'adolescent a atteint ce lundi 2 novembre 2026 la 132e place du classement mondial ATP, alors qu'il pointait au 876e rang à l'entame de cette saison 2026. Ce succès breton lui permet également d'occuper désormais la 4e place de la Race qualificative pour les Next Gen ATP Finals.

Au-delà de cette belle progression, le Francilien confirme sa réussite sur le territoire national. Moïse Kouamé affiche en effet un impressionnant ratio de 75% de victoires sur ses rencontres disputées sur le sol français. Cinq mois plus tôt, il avait déjà fait vibrer le public de Roland-Garros en atteignant le troisième tour après des victoires remarquées contre Marin Cilic puis Adolfo Daniel Vallejo, à l'issue d'une bataille de 4h56 de jeu, avant de s'incliner face à Alejandro Tabilo.

Initialement prévu pour disputer les qualifications de l'épreuve parisienne, le jeune espoir a finalement intégré directement le tableau principal grâce à une invitation libérée après le forfait de Jakub Mensik. Dans un entretien accordé à L'Équipe, Moïse Kouamé a d'ailleurs affiché une belle décontraction avant ce choc :

Toutefois, la tâche s'annonce particulièrement ardue pour le novice tricolore face à un adversaire très en forme. Alejandro Davidovich Fokina traverse la meilleure période de sa carrière sur le circuit. Classé 15e mondial selon L'Équipe, l'Espagnol reste notamment sur un sacre prestigieux décroché au Masters 1000 de Shanghai en octobre 2026, après avoir remporté les tournois de Majorque et de Chengdu durant cette saison faste.

Ce duel de haut niveau s'annonce comme une étape majeure dans l'apprentissage du prodige tricolore devant le public parisien. Le match entre Moïse Kouamé et Alejandro Davidovich Fokina est programmé ce mardi 3 novembre 2026 en deuxième rotation sur le court central de la salle de Nanterre.

#2442. Mercato : Pour renforcer sa défense, le FC Barcelone s'intéresse à un joueur de 18 ans

En quête active de renforts défensifs pour l'avenir, le FC Barcelone explore de nouvelles pistes sur le marché européen. Les dirigeants catalans s'intéressent ainsi de très près à Jordan Arnolin, jeune joueur de 18 ans évoluant sous les couleurs d'Estoril.

À en croire les informations révélées par la presse espagnole, un émissaire du club catalan avait pris place dans les tribunes de l'Estádio do Dragão, le samedi 31 octobre 2026. L'objectif était clair : observer de très près le jeune joueur d'Estoril face au FC Porto (4-0) lors de cette affiche de Liga Portugal. Une mission ciblée au Portugal.

Le FC Barcelone ne laisse rien au hasard pour préparer l'avenir de son arrière-garde. D'après le quotidien espagnol Mundo Deportivo, le superviseur barcelonais dépêché à Porto avait pour mission d'observer avec attention la prestation de Jordan Arnolin. Né le 29 avril 2008 et mesurant 1,83 m, le jeune défenseur portugais est actuellement sous contrat avec le GD Estoril Praia jusqu'au 30 juin 2029. La cellule de recrutement catalane n'a d'ailleurs pas découvert le joueur par hasard : le Barça suivait déjà ses performances lorsqu'il évoluait avec la sélection du Portugal U18, et poursuit désormais son suivi régulier chez les U19.

Face aux Dragons du FC Porto, Jordan Arnolin fêtait sa toute première titularisation en championnat cette saison, après être entré en jeu à quatre reprises lors des journées précédentes. Aligné au poste de milieu défensif, le joueur d'Estoril a disputé 62 minutes avant d'être remplacé alors que le score était de 2-0. Malgré la défaite des siens (4-0), il a compilé des chiffres notables : 26 ballons touchés, 13 passes réussies sur 15 tentées, 3 récupérations et 6 dégagements défensifs. Une copie encourageante. En effet, sa grande polyvalence séduit le Barça, qui l'envisage aussi bien en défenseur central, latéral ou sentinelle, que ce soit pour son équipe première ou son centre de formation.

Toutefois, le FC Barcelone n'est pas le seul prétendant dans ce dossier qui commence à faire parler. Jordan Arnolin, qui est le fils de l'ancien joueur Grégory Arnolin — passé notamment au Portugal par le CS Marítimo et Gil Vicente —, attise d'autres convoitises à l'étranger. Des recruteurs du LOSC Lille ainsi que du club anglais de Brighton & Hove Albion étaient également présents dans les gradins de l'Estádio do Dragão pour le superviser. La concurrence s'annonce donc bien réelle sur cette piste prometteuse, même si aucune offre formelle n'a encore été transmise par les prétendants.

Au-delà de la prospection pour le futur, la question d'une recrue immédiate se pose en Catalogne. En conférence de presse, l'entraîneur Hansi Flick a admis que le FC Barcelone ne fermait pas la porte à une arrivée en défense lors du mercato hivernal, en raison des blessures récurrentes dans ce secteur, particulièrement celles d'Andreas Christensen. Si des pistes comme Josko Gvardiol, Lisandro Martínez, Alessandro Bastoni ou le jeune Finn Jeltsch du VfB Stuttgart ont circulé, le club blaugrana s'était heurté l'été dernier au refus du FC Twente de négocier pour Ruud Nijstad. Le FC Barcelone affronte désormais Aston Villa ce mardi 3 novembre 2026 à 21h00 au Spotify Camp Nou, pour le compte de la 4e journée de la Ligue des champions.

#2441. « Déchiré par la douleur » : Tragédie en Espagne, Tenerife annonce le décès de Jesús de Miguel Alameda

Le football espagnol est sous le choc ce mardi 3 novembre 2026. Le CD Tenerife a officialisé le décès de son attaquant Jesús de Miguel Alameda, survenu à 8h00 à l'âge de 30 ans, suite à un choc survenu lundi soir avec le gardien de l'équipe adverse.

Le drame est survenu lors d'un match de la 12e journée de deuxième division espagnole (LaLiga Hypermotion), disputé le lundi 2 novembre 2026 sur la pelouse du stade Heliodoro Rodríguez López. Alors que les deux équipes se neutralisaient dans une fin de match sous tension (2-2), la rencontre face au FC Andorra a été définitivement interrompue dans le temps additionnel suite à un choc très violent entre l'attaquant de Tenerife Jesús de Miguel Alameda et le gardien du FC Andorra Jesús Owono.

Le club de Tenerife a pris la parole ce mardi matin pour annoncer la terrible nouvelle. La formation espagnole a partagé sa profonde détresse face à la perte brutale de son avant-centre. À travers un communiqué officiel publié sur X, le club a tenu à exprimer toute sa tristesse et son soutien à la famille du joueur :

L'accident s'est produit dans le temps additionnel de cette rencontre indécise. Parti en contre sur un long dégagement, Jesús de Miguel a été heurté de plein fouet au niveau du haut du corps dans le rond central par une sortie aérienne non maîtrisée du gardien andorran Jesús Owono, dont le genou droit a percuté l'attaquant. Un choc particulièrement violent.

Face à la dangerosité de l'action, l'arbitre de la rencontre a immédiatement expulsé le gardien Jesús Owono d'un carton rouge direct pour usage d'une force excessive. D'ailleurs, selon la Cadena Cope, le portier était très affecté par les conséquences de son intervention. Le match a ensuite été définitivement interrompu afin de permettre l'intervention des secours et l'évacuation rapide du joueur.

Jesús de Miguel s'est effondré inerte au sol et a subi un arrêt cardiorespiratoire sur la pelouse avant d'être pris en charge en urgence. L'attaquant a fait l'objet d'une réanimation cardio-pulmonaire pratiquée par les services médicaux à l'intérieur de l'ambulance, lui permettant de respirer à nouveau par lui-même tout en restant inconscient.

Jesús de Miguel a ensuite été admis en soins intensifs à l'Hospital Universitario Nuestra Señora de Candelaria à Santa Cruz de Tenerife dans un état jugé stable mais grave. Toutefois, la situation s'est assombrie quelques heures plus tard. Dans la nuit de lundi à mardi, le CD Tenerife avait publié un message d'alerte sur X indiquant : « L’état médical de Jesus de Miguel s’est aggravé sur le plan neurologique. Plus d’informations dans les prochaines heures. »

Au-delà des espoirs suscités par les premiers gestes de secours, le joueur de 30 ans s'est éteint au petit matin des suites de ces complications neurologiques.

#2440. « Un changement est nécessaire » : West Ham ne perd pas de temps et décide de se séparer de Nuno Espirito Santo

West Ham United a officialisé ce mardi 3 novembre 2026 le limogeage avec effet immédiat de son entraîneur principal Nuno Espírito Santo. Le club londonien a décidé de trancher dans le vif après un début de saison particulièrement poussif en Championship.

Arrivé en septembre 2025 avec un contrat de trois ans, le technicien de 52 ans n'avait pas pu empêcher la relégation des Hammers à l'issue de la saison 2025-2026. Maintenu pour guider la remontée, Nuno Espírito Santo laisse l'équipe dans une position inconfortable. Après 13 journées de Championship, West Ham ne compte que six victoires et pointe à la huitième place du classement, à six points du leader Middlesbrough. Un bilan insuffisant.

Le sort de l'entraîneur portugais s'est scellé lors de deux revers consécutifs subis à domicile au London Stadium, face à Southampton (2-3) puis contre West Bromwich Albion (1-3). Deux contre-performances de trop pour la direction. Le co-propriétaire David Sullivan souhaitait déjà se séparer de Nuno Espírito Santo l'été dernier, mais l'actionnaire principal Daniel Kretinsky avait choisi de le maintenir. Le club s'était d'ailleurs offert Arne Engels pour 22 millions de livres en provenance du Celtic, un montant record pour la Championship. Nuno Espírito Santo s'en va sur un bilan de 19 victoires, 15 nuls et 19 défaites en 53 matchs dirigés. L'entraîneur adjoint Rui Pedro Silva et l'entraîneur des gardiens Rui Barbosa quittent également leurs fonctions au sein du club.

Au-delà des résultats comptables, la fracture s'est matérialisée dans les travées du London Stadium. Pendant et après la défaite contre West Bromwich Albion, les supporters des Hammers ont clairement manifesté leur colère. Une rupture consommée avec le public. Présent en conférence de presse après le revers face à West Bromwich Albion, Nuno Espírito Santo avait tenté d'éteindre l'incendie :

Pour parer au plus pressé, West Ham a confié l'intérim à un trio composé de Mark Noble, Steve Potts et Gerard Prenderville. Toutefois, la succession avance rapidement en coulisses. Selon les révélations de David Ornstein, le club a conclu un accord avec Scott Parker, 46 ans, pour succéder à Nuno Espírito Santo. Les dirigeants londoniens espèrent qu'il sera en poste pour le déplacement à Cardiff et que Mark Noble intégrera son futur staff.

West Ham United dispute son prochain match ce mercredi 4 novembre 2026 sur la pelouse de Cardiff City, dans le cadre de la 14e journée de Championship.

#2439. Portugal : Grande première pour le fils de Cristiano Ronaldo !

C’est une étape majeure dans la jeune carrière de Cristiano Ronaldo Júnior. Lundi 2 novembre 2026, la Fédération portugaise de football a officialisé la présence de l'attaquant de 16 ans dans la liste des U17 pour disputer les éliminatoires de l'Euro 2027.

Le sélectionneur portugais Filipe Ramos a retenu le fils de Cristiano Ronaldo dans une liste de 23 joueurs dévoilée le lundi 2 novembre 2026 par la FPF. Évoluant au sein des catégories de jeunes d'Al-Nassr en Arabie saoudite, le joueur polyvalent, capable d'évoluer en pointe comme sur les ailes, totalise 3 buts en 7 apparitions cette saison sous les couleurs du club saoudien. Une belle marque de confiance. Le fils aîné de Cristiano Ronaldo franchit ainsi un palier très attendu en intégrant pour la première fois cette catégorie d'âge.

Cette arrivée chez les moins de 17 ans vient récompenser un parcours déjà très abouti avec les équipes de jeunes de la Seleção. En effet, Cristiano Ronaldo Jr avait fêté ses grands débuts internationaux le 13 mai 2025 avec les U15, catégorie avec laquelle il s'était illustré en remportant le tournoi Vlatko Markovic grâce à un doublé en finale. Promu chez les U16 dès le 30 octobre 2025, il y a compilé 3 buts en 9 matches et remporté deux compétitions, jusqu'à sa dernière sortie le 24 mai 2026. Au total, son bilan s'élève à 13 sélections et 5 buts avec le Portugal.

Même si son avenir en sélection senior n'est pas encore définitivement scellé au regard des règles de la FIFA, Cristiano Ronaldo Jr confirme sa fidélité au maillot portugais. L'attaquant de 16 ans disposait pourtant de plusieurs opportunités sur la scène internationale, puisqu'il était potentiellement sélectionnable par quatre autres nations. Né en Californie, il pouvait prétendre défendre les couleurs des États-Unis, mais aussi de l'Espagne en raison d'une résidence de plus de trois ans, de l'Angleterre après le passage de son père à Manchester, ou encore du Cap-Vert grâce aux origines de sa grand-mère paternelle. Toutefois, le joueur poursuit son chemin sous la tunique portugaise.

Le stage de préparation débutera dès le 6 novembre 2026 au centre fédéral de la Cidade do Futebol, à Oeiras dans la banlieue de Lisbonne. Pour accéder au tour suivant des qualifications de l'Euro U17 2027, le Portugal devra terminer parmi les deux premiers du groupe 6 lors des trois matches prévus à domicile contre l'Andorre le 11 novembre, la Bulgarie le 14 novembre et la Serbie le 17 novembre 2026. Au-delà des U17, le regard se tourne aussi vers Cristiano Ronaldo senior (41 ans). Après avoir purgé une suspension de 30 jours et 255 euros d'amende suite à un désaccord avec Jorge Jesus, son retour est attendu selon la presse portugaise dans la liste de l'équipe A qui sera annoncée le vendredi 6 novembre 2026.

#2437. « Je n'aime pas ce type de résultat » : la mise au point de Luis Enrique après la victoire 6-0 du PSG

Au terme de la démonstration du Paris Saint-Germain sur le terrain de Villarreal (0-6), Luis Enrique a livré une analyse très sobre en conférence de presse. Après ce large succès, l'entraîneur espagnol a confié sa gêne face à l'ampleur du score, rappelant son respect pour l'adversaire.

Mardi 3 novembre 2026, à l'Estadio de la Cerámica, le Paris Saint-Germain a signé une prestation éclatante lors de la 4e journée de la phase de ligue de la Ligue des champions. La rencontre a basculé d'entrée avec quatre buts parisiens inscrits dans les 17 premières minutes, dont trois réalisations en l'espace de cinq minutes. João Neves a ouvert le score (9e), rapidement imité par Désiré Doué (12e), Senny Mayulu (13e), Fabián Ruiz (17e, 50e) et David Boly (78e). Un récital offensif impressionnant.

Avec ce large succès (0-6), le PSG totalise 12 points en quatre matchs de phase de ligue et égale la série d'invincibilité record d'un club français en Ligue des champions, soit 14 matchs, établie par Lyon entre 2004 et 2006.

Présent devant les journalistes après la victoire 6-0 à Villarreal, Luis Enrique a confié son embarras face à l'ampleur du score : « Je n'aime pas ce type de résultat », soulignant sa peine de voir son adversaire dans une telle détresse. L'entraîneur du PSG a insisté sur le fait que son équipe respecte toujours l'adversaire en jouant avec la même intensité tout le match sans fermer le jeu, citant en exemple la finale de Ligue des champions remportée face à l'Inter Milan.

Au-delà du score, cette soirée a été marquée par des moments forts en émotion. En effet, Luis Enrique a adressé ses condoléances au CD Tenerife et à la famille du joueur Jesús de Miguel après son décès tragique. D'ailleurs, Fabián Ruiz a lui aussi rendu hommage à l'attaquant dès le coup de sifflet final au micro de Canal+.

Malgré cette démonstration européenne, Luis Enrique a tenu à calmer l'euphorie ambiante en rappelant que rien n'était acquis et que l'objectif premier demeurait le top 8. L'entraîneur a notamment prévenu : « nous ne sommes pas encore champions, ni en finale à Madrid ». Pas question de relâcher la pression.

Toutefois, les Parisiens doivent rapidement basculer sur les affaires courantes. Le prochain match du Paris Saint-Germain est programmé le samedi 7 novembre 2026 à 20h45 au Parc des Princes face à l'ESTAC Troyes en Ligue 1.
